annotations.description: Casting Hired Claw before combat is suboptimal. The opponent has only two Spirebluff Canals (UU or UR open) and could have Spell Snare (counters MV 2 spells) or other interaction. More importantly, casting creatures before combat when you have combat tricks or want to preserve information is generally worse. Here, Burnout Bashtronaut has menace and the opponent has no blockers, so attacking first would deal damage, potentially trigger speed increases, and then post-combat you could cast Hired Claw with full information. Additionally, if the opponent had a way to punish overextension, playing the creature pre-combat gives them more information about your board before you attack. The Rockface Village activation (+1/+0 and haste to a Lizard) is sorcery-speed only, so if the plan was to give the new Hired Claw haste via Rockface Village, that would require tapping Rockface Village and paying R - but all mana sources appear tapped except Rockface Village. Actually, Rockface Village is untapped and could tap for R to cast Hired Claw, then there's no mana left for the activation. So the Hired Claw won't attack this turn anyway. The correct sequence is: attack with Burnout Bashtronaut first (menace, no blockers = free damage, advances speed), then cast Hired Claw post-combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hired Claw pre-combat in the precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Burnout Bashtronaut first (opponent has no blockers, menace is irrelevant, free damage advances speed counter), then cast Hired Claw in the post-combat main phase

annotations.description: Gem3P Stoic declined to cast Burst Lightning in response to Hired Claw being cast. Hired Claw is a 1/2 Lizard that deals 1 damage whenever Lizards attack, and can grow with +1/+1 counters. The opponent already has Burnout Bashtronaut on board, so the Hired Claw's Lizard attack trigger won't fire (Bashtronaut is a Goblin, not a Lizard), but Hired Claw itself is a Lizard and will trigger its own ability when it attacks. However, Burst Lightning costs R and would use one of only two available lands, leaving Gem3P unable to hold up Spell Snare on the opponent's turn. With two Spell Snares in hand and only two lands, preserving the mana for a potential counter next turn is defensible. Still, letting Hired Claw resolve means it can start growing and dealing incremental damage, and Burst Lightning kills it cleanly. The decision to not remove it is debatable since the opponent could play more Lizards or use Hired Claw's pump ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Burst Lightning targeting Hired Claw, allowing it to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Burst Lightning targeting Hired Claw to remove it before it can accumulate value. Alternatively, waiting to see if a higher-priority target appears is reasonable, but Hired Claw's incremental damage and growth potential make it a reasonable removal target.

annotations.description: Gem3P Stoic passed on casting Opt during their precombat main phase with 2 untapped lands and no other plays worth making this turn. While holding up Spell Snare is reasonable, the opponent's board already has multiple threats deployed (two Hired Claws and a Burnout Bashtronaut), and the opponent's lands are all tapped. Casting Opt now would help dig toward answers (like finding a third land drop or removal) while the opponent can't cast anything meaningful. Additionally, Opt in the graveyard reduces Eddymurk Crab's cost. The player still needs to play a land this turn (Multiversal Passage or Riverpyre Verge), so they could cast Opt, then play their land and still have mana available. However, saving Spell Snare mana for the opponent's turn has some value, making this debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Opt or Burst Lightning during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Opt to dig for answers and fuel Eddymurk Crab's cost reduction, then play a land. With opponent tapped out, there's minimal risk. Could also consider Burst Lightning on Burnout Bashtronaut before it reaches max speed, though saving it may be reasonable.

annotations.description: Casting Sleight of Hand (a sorcery) instead of Opt (an instant) during the main phase is suboptimal for two reasons: (1) Opt could be cast at end of opponent's turn, leaving mana open for Spell Snare during the opponent's turn 3, which is a critical tempo window. By casting Sleight of Hand now, they use their mana proactively and lose the ability to hold up Spell Snare this turn cycle. (2) However, they have two Spell Snares and only one untapped land would remain either way after casting a 1-mana spell and playing Multiversal Passage tapped — actually, they have 3 lands and could play Multiversal Passage as their land drop. If they play Passage (paying 2 life for untapped or letting it enter tapped) they'd have 4 mana sources. But the key issue is: they should save their instant-speed card draw (Opt) for the opponent's end step and cast the sorcery now if they must cast something now. Wait — that's actually what they did. Sleight of Hand is a sorcery so it MUST be cast on their own turn. Opt is an instant that could be saved. So casting Sleight of Hand now and saving Opt for later is actually correct sequencing. Let me reconsider... The question is whether they should cast anything at all right now or hold up Spell Snare mana. They have 3 lands and haven't played a land yet. If they play Multiversal Passage untapped (paying 2 life), they'd have 4 lands, enough to cast Sleight of Hand AND hold up Spell Snare. So the play of Sleight of Hand now is fine if they also play the land. Actually, looking more carefully, the decision is specifically between Sleight of Hand and Opt — both cost {U}. Casting the sorcery now and saving the instant for later is correct. This isn't a blunder.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sleight of Hand during main phase
annotations.betterLine: This is actually correct sequencing — cast the sorcery now, save the instant Opt for opponent's end step

annotations.description: Gem3P Stoic chose Winternight Stories over Island from Sleight of Hand. They already have 3 lands in play and Multiversal Passage in hand (which can come in untapped for 2 life), so they'll have 4 mana next turn. However, they need to hit land drops to eventually cast Eddymurk Crab (7 mana, reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard - currently 2 in graveyard so it costs 5). Taking Island would ensure a smooth 4th land drop without paying life for Multiversal Passage, and would enable holding up both Spell Snares more comfortably. Winternight Stories is a powerful draw spell but costs 3 mana and requires discarding, and the player already has a decent hand with reactive spells. The choice is defensible since Winternight Stories provides card advantage and fills the graveyard to reduce Eddymurk Crab's cost, but taking the Island to guarantee the land drop and preserve life total against an aggressive opponent with menace and haste creatures could have been better.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Winternight Stories over Island from Sleight of Hand
annotations.betterLine: Take Island to guarantee the 4th land drop without paying 2 life from Multiversal Passage, keeping options open against the aggressive opponent while still having Multiversal Passage for turn 5

annotations.description: Failed to play a land before casting Tersa Lightshatter. Both Mountain and Rockface Village were available as land drops. Playing a land first is strictly better sequencing — it doesn't change what can be cast but ensures the land drop isn't forgotten, and Rockface Village specifically provides utility to pump Hired Claw (a Lizard). The player's reasoning incorrectly stated they couldn't play a land.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tersa Lightshatter without first making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Rockface Village (or Mountain) first, then cast Tersa Lightshatter for {2}{R}. Rockface Village is preferred as it can pump Hired Claw with its activated ability.

annotations.description: Discarding Nova Hellkite instead of Rockface Village as part of Tersa Lightshatter's ETB discard-then-draw effect. Nova Hellkite is a powerful 4/5 flying haste finisher that can also be warped for 2R. While keeping a land drop is reasonable to avoid mana issues, the player already has 3 lands in play and Tersa is drawing replacement cards. Nova Hellkite represents a much higher power level card than a utility land, and with an aggressive board of Bashtronaut, Hired Claw, and Tersa already applying pressure, having a 5-drop finisher (or a 3-mana warp option) could be more valuable than a 4th land that only adds colorless/red creature mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Nova Hellkite, keeping Rockface Village for the land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Rockface Village instead, keeping Nova Hellkite as a high-impact threat that can be warped for 2R as early as next turn or hard-cast on turn 5. The aggressive board state suggests closing the game quickly is more important than an incremental land drop.

annotations.description: Casting Winternight Stories (3 mana sorcery) on turn 4 taps out the player, leaving no mana to hold up the two Spell Snares in hand. The opponent has Hired Claw in the graveyard and could cast 2-mana threats. Additionally, at 12 life facing an aggressive board (Burnout Bashtronaut, Hired Claw, Tersa Lightshatter all attacking), spending the entire turn drawing cards rather than holding up interaction is risky. Casting Opt at end of opponent's turn would leave up Spell Snare mana and still dig for answers, though Winternight Stories does draw more cards. The opponent's creatures are all tapped, so there's some safety, but the player also needs to find answers quickly and Winternight Stories requires discarding 2 cards (unless discarding a creature), which could be costly.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Winternight Stories for 3 mana, tapping out on turn 4
annotations.betterLine: Hold up mana for Spell Snare and cast Opt at end of opponent's turn, or play Multiversal Passage first then evaluate whether to tap out for Winternight Stories with 4 lands available (keeping 1 up for Spell Snare)
